# Phase 03 — Harness Seam, CLI Door, And The Two Proofs (ADR-007, V-012)

Context: with Phase 02 the inline class exists. This phase adds the single
domain seam, the CLI door, and runs both consumers live so the foundation
claim is recorded from persisted evidence, not narrative.

## Requirements

- R1 Seam. `domains/coding/harness/enrich-and-validate-contract.mjs` exporting
  pure `enrichAndValidateContract(contract, { domain, work })`. For a Work at a
  declared stage it: requires `contract.supports` to be an operation id in
  `operationsForStage(domain, work.stage)` (reject otherwise); adds
  `contextRefs` (CONTEXT.md, plan.md via `resolveContentRoot`); adds an
  allowed-scope constraint (repository read scope); sets the coding read-only
  evidence rule (`reported` requires `agent-report.md` artifact); writes
  role->tier hints into `policy` (same shape as `op.policy` merge today). It
  never sets executor ids. Foundation calls it from `buildAssignment` between
  the generic validator and the normalizer when `domain` is present.
- R2 Non-driving rule. `chooseStageOperation` / `findLatestAssignmentRunResult`
  ignore Assignments with `provenance.kind === 'inline'` when looking for a
  stage verdict; add an explicit filter with a test.
- R3 CLI door. `src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs` `execute` gains `--contract <file>`
  (JSON). Mutually exclusive with `--for`/stage flags. Prints assignment id,
  run id, RunResult path. No new verb. User-visible: add a `## [Unreleased]`
  line to `CHANGELOG.md`; no new config default or env var is introduced (if
  one becomes necessary, register it with `fgos setup`/`doctor` per AGENTS.md).
- R4 Proof 1 (standalone). Contract: role `reviewer`, objective = one bounded
  design question about a doc in this repo, `mutation: read-only`,
  `evidence.required: reported`, `timeoutMs`, `maxRuns: 1`, caller writer id.
  Executor via policy hint `preferExecutor: claude-reviewer` (configured in
  `.fgos/config.json`, read-only-scoped `claude -p` spawn) with a sonnet-class
  model; `decide --for` purposes do not include reviewer roles, so the proof
  must go through `execute --contract`, never `decide --for`. Record under
  `docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/step-07-mvp/proof-1-standalone-inline-read-only.md`:
  command transcript, `assignment.json`, `runs/01/{run,dispatch-plan,result}.json`,
  and the assertion that no field references a coding stage/TaskSpec.
- R5 Proof 2 (coding consult). Throwaway Work at `planning` with a real
  CONTEXT.md/plan.md. Contract: role `advisor`, `supports: shape-plan`,
  objective "are plan.md's steps consistent with the locked decisions in
  CONTEXT.md", read-only, `reported`. Record under
  `verification/step-07-mvp/proof-2-coding-consult-supporting-planning-work.md`:
  harness-added refs/constraints visible in `assignment.json`, RunResult, and
  proof that `fgos list` shows the Work's stage/status unchanged and the
  driver's next operation choice ignored the inline result.
- R6 Traceability: extend the track's existing
  `verification/step-07-mvp/index.md` (the master's status board) with an
  "ADR Traceability" section: one row per ADR-006/007 clause -> test or proof
  path. Proof records for R4/R5 live under `verification/step-07-mvp/proofs/<cell-id>/`
  with the markdown summaries named in R4/R5 beside them.

## Files

Create: `domains/coding/harness/enrich-and-validate-contract.mjs` + test;
verification records above.
Modify: `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs` (seam call), `operation-choice.mjs`
(R2 filter), `src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs` (R3), `bin/fgos.mjs` only if the
dispatch subcommand wiring requires the new flag to be declared there.

## Tests

- Seam unit: rejects missing/illegal `supports`; adds refs; never sets
  executor; identical output for identical input (purity).
- R2: an inline Assignment with a READY-looking claim on a planning Work does
  not advance the edge; a declared `validate-plan` READY still does.
- CLI: `--contract` with a mutating contract exits non-zero before launch;
  `--contract` + `--for` rejected.
- Live: Proof 1 and Proof 2 executed out-of-process (no fake executor), same
  standard as Step 06 Cells 6.3/final.

## Risks / Rollback

- Proof 2 needs a real executor run; budget it (one run each, sonnet tier).
- If Proof 1 and Proof 2 require different build/dispatch/result code paths to
  pass, stop: the foundation boundary is not found — record it in the
  checkpoint rather than patching around it.
- Rollback: seam and flag are additive; revert PR.

# Step 08 - Standalone Coordination And Reusable Group Cognition

Status: done | Created: 2026-09-01 | Completed: 2026-09-02 | Owner: maintainer

All 8 phases closed. Full execution trace, review history (including
every real bug found and fixed, and both proof-rigor gaps found and
closed in the plan's own final cell), and the closing Deferral Audit
live under `docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/step-08-standalone-coordination/`
(`index.md` is the entry point; `deferral-audit.md` is the final
AC-I001-I009 closure record).
Execution track: `step-08-standalone-coordination`

Authority entering the plan:

- [Agent Coordination Vision](../../docs/architect/agent-coordination/vision.md)
- [ADR-006](../../docs/architect/agent-coordination/decisions/ADR-006-assignment-provenance-and-contract-snapshot.md)
- [ADR-007](../../docs/architect/agent-coordination/decisions/ADR-007-domain-harness-seam-and-non-driving-inline-evidence.md)
- [Intent Preservation Ledger](../../docs/architect/agent-coordination/intent-preservation-ledger.md)
- human-approved decisions in the [Step 08 checkpoint](../../docs/architect/agent-coordination/proposals/step-08-standalone-coordination-protocols.md#discussion-checkpoint-step-08-recommended-decisions-and-plan-2026-09-01)
- reconciled [pre-plan architecture review](../reports/reviewer-260901-1403-GH-07-step08-pre-plan-architecture-review.md)

Phase 00 extracts the approved checkpoint into accepted ADRs, contracts,
architecture, vocabulary, and the runner area spec before feature code relies on
it. The proposal remains rationale and discussion history, never runtime
authority.

## Goal

Deliver one domain-neutral coordination foundation that can run:

1. agent-led standalone coordination with no predeclared protocol;
2. declared reusable coordination through a typed `CoordinationProtocol`;
3. deterministic heterogeneous cohorts across provider/model/tier policy;
4. one real Group Cognition framework using divergent, critical, evidence, and
   convergent activities;
5. interactive and headless operation over the same semantic engine.

Every execution-triggering activity must converge on the existing
`Assignment -> DispatchPlan -> Run -> RunResult -> evidence` core. Work,
Workflow, Mission, and a declared protocol remain optional. Work remains the
only delivery lifecycle authority when present.

## Locked Product Decisions

- `CoordinationSession` is the V1 executable/recovery root. Future `Mission`
  may reference N sessions but is `deferred-preserved`; V1 has no mandatory or
  dead `missionId`.
- `FlowDefinition` is the shared versioned graph/operation/policy IR. Typed
  profiles preserve different semantics: `Workflow` uses Stage;
  `CoordinationProtocol` uses Phase. Existing Workflow behavior is projected
  additively; it is not migrated onto a new runtime in this step.
- Schema uses `role` and `actors`. Role, seat, and responsibility position are
  one concept. `SessionActor` is an addressable instance filling a Role.
  `Persona` is behavioral identity; `Stance` is a temporary viewpoint and is
  not a V1 schema field.
- Definitions/domain packages own Role responsibilities and legal actor slots.
  A trusted run request may bind a SessionActor slot to Persona and execution
  policy, or populate declared multiplicity, but cannot silently change that
  slot's Role or an operation's responsibility. Agent-led sessions may propose
  new actors/roles only through the same foundation validator and bounds.
- Declared protocol is optional. Agent-led sessions may create bounded inline
  Assignments dynamically without `protocolId`, Work, Stage, or TaskSpec.
- Portable definitions express WHAT through role, capabilities, evidence,
  mutation, context, tier floors, topology, and hard cohort constraints. They
  do not pin concrete executors or literal models.
- Trusted operator/session policy may express global or per-actor execution
  preferences. Governance remains final. A hard CLI executor selection means
  "highest-priority human preference subject to validation/governance", not a
  bypass.
- `purpose` routing, executor fitness scoring, autonomous provider routing,
  organization overlays, first-class AgentMessage, general AdhocTask storage,
  unrestricted peer chat, and a framework marketplace are out of V1.
- `.fgos/coordination/` is gitignored local runtime/recovery state. Verification
  exports selected evidence deliberately.
- Mission-lite is replaced directly. There is no migration reader, detector,
  reporter, compatibility writer, or stored-data migration. Assignment
  construction also drops its prototype `missionId` input; a future Mission
  groups completed session ids from above instead of entering Assignment.
- Interactive ships first for explicit observation. Headless later invokes the
  same session/protocol/dispatch/evidence/recovery engine. Visibility and
  operator presence are the intended differences; telemetry is deferred.
- Standalone proofs are read-only. Work-attached mutation is a stop gate until
  a coding-domain proof demonstrates domain-owned worktree/resource isolation,
  merge ownership, recovery, and Work transition authority.

## Phases

| # | Phase | Depends on | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | [Canonical contracts and dispatch prerequisites](phase-00-canonical-contracts-and-dispatch-prerequisites.md) | Step 07 complete | Accepted design surface; executor/provider/tier resolution is truthful and CLI-reachable |
| 01 | [CoordinationSession ledger and agent-led proof](phase-01-coordination-session-and-agent-led-proof.md) | 00 | Persistent standalone session resumes without duplicate Assignments and dynamically consults one actor |
| 02 | [Shared FlowDefinition kernel and typed profiles](phase-02-shared-flow-definition-kernel.md) | 01 | Existing Workflow and protocol fixtures normalize through one additive IR with profile isolation |
| 03 | [Declared consult protocol](phase-03-declared-consult-protocol.md) | 02 | Declared and agent-led consult use one governed engine with equivalent evidence semantics |
| 04 | [Research fan-out/fan-in and Cohort Planner](phase-04-research-cohort-planner.md) | 03 | Explainable heterogeneous allocation, isolated branches, verified fan-in, loud unsatisfied constraints |
| 05 | [First Group Cognition framework](phase-05-group-cognition-framework.md) | 04 | Real external-project comparison records quality gain or honest null result with dissent preserved |
| 06 | [Recovery, partial completion, and budget hardening](phase-06-recovery-partial-completion-and-budgets.md) | 05 | Crash, retry, quorum, bounds, leakage, and evidence-laundering attacks are negatively proven |
| 07 | [Headless parity, CLI stabilization, and adoption](phase-07-headless-parity-cli-and-adoption.md) | 06 | Public CLI/API stable; interactive/headless semantic parity proven; final intent audit closed |

Phases execute strictly in this order. Do not combine Phase 00 dispatch work
with coordination runtime, and do not extract the shared kernel before the
agent-led session proves the minimal runtime shape.

## Plan-Level Acceptance

- Full `npm test` passes relative to the exact baseline recorded before P00.1;
  no baseline failure may grow or be reclassified without evidence.
- Accepted ADRs/contracts and `docs/specs/runner.md` describe the implemented
  public behavior; the Step 08 proposal points to them and remains non-normative.
- A standalone session succeeds with `workId: null`, no Workflow, no Stage, no
  TaskSpec, and no protocol id.
- Existing coding Workflow behavior and golden tests remain unchanged while a
  `CoordinationProtocol` uses the same neutral IR.
- No coordinator, protocol, profile, role, actor, Skill, or Cohort Planner
  spawns an executor directly or creates a private dispatch/evidence path.
- Assignment/Run/RunResult remain canonical records. Session state stores
  references and field-level policy provenance, not copied truth.
- Actual executor id, provider family, model, tier, policy sources, and
  governance result are persisted for every live actor run.
- At least two configured provider families support every policy tier used by
  the Phase 05 framework. Missing support stops the live proof; it is never
  faked or silently weakened.
- Independent branches cannot read sibling outputs before fan-in. Synthesis
  cannot upgrade `reported`, failed, stale, or foreign evidence to `verified`.
- Missing required actors block completion unless an explicit partial policy
  is satisfied; every omission and dissenting result remains visible.
- Interactive and headless doors invoke the same engine and produce
  semantically equivalent persisted records for the same deterministic fixture.
- No Step 08 proof mutates a consuming repository or advances/merges Work.
- The final Deferral Audit covers AC-I001 through AC-I009 and includes an
  executable must-not-preclude proof for every entry touched by the plan.

## Intent Traceability

| Intent | Implemented or advanced here | Executable must-not-preclude proof |
|---|---|---|
| AC-I001 | Persistent standalone CoordinationSession | Run with null Work and no lifecycle fields; reject any universal Work/Stage requirement |
| AC-I002 | Dynamic primary-to-specialist consult | Run session with no protocol id; prove declared definitions remain optional |
| AC-I003 | Consult, research, Group Cognition protocols | Static/runtime test that all protocol execution reaches `executeAssignment` and no direct spawn exists |
| AC-I004 | Heterogeneous cohort and cognitive activities | Two-provider required-tier allocation plus dissent/evidence-aware synthesis tests |
| AC-I005 | Shared kernel and project/domain discovery seams | Normalize packaged and project-owned fixtures through one loader; no foundation fork |
| AC-I006 | Corrected dispatch provenance and one core | Unknown executor/provider-tier fail closed; all runs persist resolver provenance; no private dispatch core |
| AC-I007 | Mission remains optional future grouping | Session manifest schema rejects `missionId`; a pure future-grouping fixture can reference N session ids without rewriting them |
| AC-I008 | Interactive first, then headless capability parity | Same deterministic request through both doors yields equivalent semantic records after visibility fields are normalized |
| AC-I009 | Domain isolation boundary preserved | Concurrent mutating actors sharing one workspace are refused; no merge/Work-transition API exists in coordination engine |

Each phase closes with the ledger's Deferral Audit template. A status changes to
`implemented` only when its accepted contract and named proof both exist.

## Out Of Scope / Do Not Build

- Mission identity, persistence, aggregation, or migration compatibility.
- Mutating standalone coordination and Work-attached mutating live execution.
- Work lifecycle transitions, branch creation, merge, approval, or worktree
  allocation inside `src/runner/coordination/**`.
- A second execution core, direct `spawn`, private provider SDK, or protocol-
  specific executor adapter.
- General task-category/`purpose` routing, weighted scoring, learned routing,
  cost optimization, or automatic credential probing.
- Literal executor/model pins in portable `CoordinationProtocol` files.
- Full provider-by-tier matrix; only tiers a chosen framework requires matter.
- First-class AgentMessage, free peer chat, recursive/unbounded task creation,
  framework marketplace, organization overlay SDK, UI/dashboard, telemetry
  backend, or herdr-spawn proof.
- Consumer migration for the current Workflow runtime. The adapter is additive.

## Autonomous Execution Contract

Use the [Master Multi-Agent Implementation Coordinator](../../docs/architect/agent-coordination/playbooks/prompts/master-coordinator.md).
This plan contains no open product decision. Routine implementation choices are
delegated to the master using repository precedent and the smallest compatible
change. The master must not ask for confirmation between cells.

Stop only when one of these objective gates occurs:

1. an accepted source above contradicts a requirement and no additive
   interpretation exists;
2. full or focused tests cannot run because required local infrastructure is
   unavailable after one documented recovery attempt;
3. a required independent Reviewer or Red-Team cannot be launched;
4. a required live CLI executor/provider is absent, unconfigured, lacks the
   exact required tier, or fails authentication after one bounded retry;
5. the external consuming-project case cannot be selected before observing
   candidate outputs;
6. Work-attached mutation becomes necessary to satisfy a requirement;
7. GitNexus reports HIGH/CRITICAL impact and the active cell did not already
   name that blast radius and mitigation;
8. concurrent/user changes overlap an active cell such that preservation is
   impossible without choosing whose behavior wins.

Do not stop for naming, file placement, test-fixture shape, error wording,
internal helper boundaries, or other reversible choices already constrained by
the phase. Infer those from adjacent code and record them in the cell trace.

PLAN_DIR: /home/vantt/projects/forgentX/plans/260901-1542-step08-standalone-coordination

  - docs/architect/agent-coordination/decisions/ADR-007-domain-harness-seam-and-non-driving-inline-evidence.md

Before P00.1, the master records `git status`, preserves all unrelated changes,

# Doer report — P00.4: provider-family derivation disagreement fix

Branch: `step-08-standalone-coordination`, base `75505c75812703b355f1291d618244c75a5d7b09`, HEAD after fix `454ecb56`.

## What was fixed

**Fix 1 — `src/runner/dispatch/assignment-policy.mjs:~213`** (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`'s `resolvedProvider` computation): the single-argument `deriveProviderFamily(registeredExecutorEntry)` call silently defaulted its `resolvedCommand` parameter to `'claude'`, disagreeing with `resolve.mjs:429`'s correct two-argument call for any registered executor with no `providerModel`/`provider` field whose real command isn't a Claude CLI command (live-confirmed: `codex-cli`, `codex-herdr`, `herdr`).

Fix extracts the real command the same way `resolve.mjs`'s `resolveExecutorConfig` does — `registeredExecutorEntry.invocations.find(inv => inv.via === 'cli')?.command` — and passes it as the second argument. Every currently-registered production executor (`.fgos/config.json`'s `runner.executors`) is `invocations[]`-shaped, so this covers the real bug fully. A bare (non-`invocations[]`) entry shape has no such structured signal, so `registeredExecutorCommand` stays `undefined` there and `deriveProviderFamily`'s own default parameter (`'claude'`) applies — byte-identical to the pre-fix behavior for that shape. This mattered: an initial version of the fix that also read a bare entry's flat `.command` field regressed ~20 tests across `test/runner/assignment-runresult.test.mjs`, `operation-choice.test.mjs`, `mission-lite.test.mjs`, etc. — those fixtures register a fake executor under the id `claude` with `command: process.execPath` (a locally-swapped-in Node binary standing in for the real CLI, common test convention), which is not a real provider signal. Restricting the extraction to the structured `invocations[]` shape avoided that regression while still fixing the real bug and preserving the deliberately-different `custom-claude-executor` test (bare shape, `command: 'claude'`, expects family `'claude'` via `deriveProviderFamily`'s own default).

**Fix 2 — `src/runner/dispatch/transport.mjs:~169`** (`resolveExecutorCommand`'s returned `provider` field, consumed by `cli.mjs`'s stderr dispatch banners and `loop.mjs`'s `executor.dispatch` audit event): was `executor.provider ?? executor.command` — for every currently-registered production executor (no top-level `.provider` alias declared anywhere in `.fgos/config.json`), this always fell through to the raw `executor.command`, ignoring `providerModel` entirely (e.g. `glm-cli`, routed to `z-ai`/OpenRouter via env override, would show `provider=claude` in the banner — actively misleading).

Fix changes the fallback to `executor.governance.providerFamily` (`resolveExecutorConfig`'s own already-computed `deriveProviderFamily(executorEntry, executor.command)` result). An explicit `executor.provider` display alias still wins first — this is a deliberate, separately-tested concept distinct from the model-routing family (`dispatch.test.mjs:3230`, "D9's reported agy/Gemini bug" regression test: an executor can alias to `"agy"` for display while its real family/model-routing `providerModel` is `"gemini"`). Read current-cell.md, P00.3.md in full (Proof Matrix, Commands, Review,
Fix Evidence), the phase-00 plan's R9-R11 text, both live-proof logs, the
full `--assignment`/`--contract` branches of `src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs`
including `findDuplicateOverrideFlag()`, the `feature.yaml` diff, and all
touched test files. Built a standalone repro script
(`redteam-probe.mjs`, in the session scratchpad, not committed) that spawns
`node src/runner/dispatch.mjs execute ...` as a real subprocess against a
temp `.fgos/config.json` with a harmless echo executor, mirroring the
existing test suite's own `mkTempDir()`/`writeEchoExecutor()` pattern —
every finding below is demonstrated by a real CLI invocation, never a mock
or a static-analysis guess.

## Findings

1. **HIGH — `findDuplicateOverrideFlag()` misses a duplicate flag when the
   second occurrence is the very last token in argv.** The helper's loop
   bound (`i < rest.length - 1`) excludes exactly one array index — the
   literal last element — regardless of whether that occurrence "has a
   following value," contradicting the Fix Evidence's own description of
   the mechanism. Reproduced: `--executor named_executor --executor` (bare,
   trailing) dispatches successfully (exit 0) instead of being rejected.
   Practical harm is bounded (`flagValue`'s `indexOf` still picks the first
   value, so no wrong executor is silently substituted), but it is a real,
   live gap against R9's literal "reject duplicate ... before launch" text.

2. **MEDIUM — the same helper has a false-positive mode.** A value that
   happens to literally equal another flag's name string (e.g. `--tier`
   given no real value, immediately followed by a genuine single
   `--executor foo`) triggers a false "duplicate flag" rejection, because
   the checker does raw string-equality across all of `rest` with no
   concept of flag-vs-value position. Confirms `flagValue()` and
   `findDuplicateOverrideFlag()` disagree on what counts as "a flag
   occurrence."

3. **HIGH — P00.4's claimed durable tracking does not exist.** The
   Coordinator disposition says the deferred HIGH `deriveProviderFamily`
   finding "is fixed via a small dedicated follow-up cell (P00.4) ... See
   index.md for the P00.4 entry." `index.md` has zero occurrences of
   "P00.4" and zero mention of the deferred defect anywhere. The only
   record is this file's own prose. If index.md's Cell Log isn't updated
   with a real P00.4 row before this cell closes, the disclosed governance
   hole has no durable trail.

4. **MEDIUM — a third, previously-unflagged `deriveProviderFamily`-family
   bug, live-reproduced in the glm-cli proof log's own quoted evidence.**
   `transport.mjs:163`'s `provider: executor.provider ?? executor.command`
   reads a dead config field (`provider` — zero of 12 registered executors
   set it; everyone uses `providerModel`) and falls through to the literal
   command name, ignoring the already-correctly-computed
   `executor.governance.providerFamily` sitting on the same object. Live
   effect: the glm-cli proof log's own stderr banner reads
   `provider=claude` when the real provider family is `z-ai` — the
   Reviewer quoted this line verbatim without explaining the discrepancy.
   Confirmed the blast radius is confined to the stderr banner and the bare
   (non-R9) `dispatch execute <executorId>` door's own RunResult — R11's
   specific proof-required RunResult fields for the `--assignment`/
   `--contract` doors are not corrupted (`assignment-runner.mjs` never
   forwards `rawResult.provider`/`.command` into the persisted

   P00.3 (`transport.mjs` absent from this cell's diff). Same root-cause
   family as finding HIGH already disclosed in P00.3's Review section —
   should be folded into the same P00.4 scope.

  duplicate-flag check: confirmed a real empty directory is left behind on

  `findDuplicateOverrideFlag()` at all, or whether the CLI's whitespace-
  separated convention should just be documented as the only supported
  form — a product decision, not something this red-team pass resolves.

# Red-Team re-check: P01.1 round-2 crash-safety fixes

Scope: focused re-verification of `createSessionAssignment` /
`completeAssignmentRegistration` in `src/runner/coordination/store.mjs`,
after the round-1 (write-order) and round-2 (self-heal + taskKey hashing +
inner-crash-window) fixes. Did not re-run the original full attack list
(contract fidelity, session-blindness, etc.) — already covered twice.

## What was verified

1. **Re-derived the crash-point induction independently.** Listed every
   sequential on-disk write `createSessionAssignment` performs (5 writes:
   directory claim, claim-file, `assignment.json`, event append, ref
   update), then hand-traced the actual code (not the doc comment) for
   every crash point between them. All converge to one of: true existing
   Assignment, safe loud `CoordinationError`, or completed self-heal. None
   produces a silent duplicate Assignment, silent duplicate event, or a
   permanently session-invisible Assignment.
2. **Reproduced 2 novel crash windows independently**, via a standalone
   script (`/tmp/.../redteam-recheck-p01-1.mjs`, not the shipped test
   file) calling the real exported functions against hand-constructed
   on-disk state:
   - Inner self-heal crash window (event appended, ref missing, inside
     `completeAssignmentRegistration`): self-heals correctly, no
     duplicate event. Also proved a genuinely duplicated event line IS
     detectable via `readSessionEvents` (so the "stays at 1" result is
     the guard doing real work, not a blind spot).
   - taskKey-hash mismatch/collision throw path (`store.mjs:389-394`):
     **zero coverage in the shipped test suite** — independently
     constructed a decoy claim file and confirmed a named
     `CoordinationError` (`category: "validation"`), no side effects.
3. Confirmed `completeAssignmentRegistration` is unexported and only
   called from the two sites inside `createSessionAssignment`'s own held
   `withEventsLock` — genuinely never reachable outside the lock.
4. Confirmed the taskKey-hashing function (`hashTaskKey`, SHA-256 prefix)
   and independently confirmed `"primary-round-1"` / `"primary_round_1"`
   hash to distinct values — the MEDIUM fix's regression test is not
   self-defeating.
5. Ran the full required test command (758 pass, 0 fail) and the smoke
   check (`mechanism` field present). Confirmed the contract doc's
   Storage Layout table lists `tasks/<hash>.json`. Confirmed
   `git status --porcelain -- src test domains
   docs/architect/agent-coordination/contracts/` shows only files this
   cell's full history (both fix rounds) claims.

## New finding (LOW, informational, not blocking)

`store.mjs:388`'s claim-file `JSON.parse` is unguarded — unlike its
sibling `readAssignmentJson` (`store.mjs:254-262`), which wraps its own
`JSON.parse` and rethrows `CoordinationError('corrupt-log', ...)`. A crash
mid-write of the claim file itself (a torn `fs.writeFileSync` on
`tasks/<hash>.json`) leaves a claim file that exists but fails to parse.
Independently reproduced: a truncated claim file causes
`createSessionAssignment` to throw a raw, unwrapped `SyntaxError`
(`instanceof CoordinationError` is `false`, `category` is `undefined`),
not the module's own error taxonomy. This is still a safe loud (and
permanent, same as the already-accepted claim-only crash window) failure
— never a silent duplicate or further corruption — so it doesn't violate
the specific safety bar this re-check was scoped to, but it breaks the
module's own fail-closed `CoordinationError` convention. Smallest fix:
wrap `store.mjs:388`'s `JSON.parse` the same way `readAssignmentJson`
already does.

Also noted (informational only): the inter-write window between the
Assignment-directory claim and the claim-file write can leave a harmless
orphaned *empty* directory on retry (never becomes a real Assignment, not
referenced anywhere) — safe, but not named in the function's doc comment
alongside its two sibling crash windows. And `completeAssignmentRegistration`'s
duplicate-check does a full `readEvents` scan on every call (including the
common first-time path), a mechanism deviation from `state/store.mjs`'s
incremental-view convention (tsk-49e) — low practical risk since a
session's own event log is scoped to that session, not the whole
platform's history.

## Verdict

**FIX CONFIRMED — READY TO CLOSE.** Both the HIGH (phantom
never-registered Assignment) and MEDIUM (taskKey collision) fixes hold
under independent hand-tracing and independent reproduction. One new LOW
finding recorded in the verification doc for the maintainer's awareness;
does not block closure.

Full detail appended to
`docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/step-08-standalone-coordination/P01.1.md`
under "### Red-Team re-check (round-2 fixes, crash-safety focus)".

Status: DONE
Summary: Independently re-derived and reproduced the crash-safety
induction for `createSessionAssignment`'s self-heal/taskKey-hash fixes —
holds correctly under every traced crash point and 2 independently
reproduced novel cases. Filed one new LOW (unguarded claim-file
`JSON.parse`), non-blocking.
Concerns/Blockers: none blocking; LOW finding is a one-line suggested fix
for a future pass if desired.

- Do not modify or loosen
  `core/coordination-protocols/group-cognition-framework.yaml`.
- Do not introduce an autonomous in-graph coordinator/leader.
- Do not give Agent Coordination Work lifecycle, git, worktree, merge, approval,
  or coding-domain mutation authority.
- Do not create a second execution core or private evidence path.
- Do not reinterpret retry as recheck. Retry supersedes a Run for one
  Assignment; recheck creates a new Assignment against new artifact/evidence.
- Do not use playbook prose as runtime logic. The Master Prompt remains a
  manual implementation coordinator and proof source only.

## Phases

|---|---|---|---|---|

the implementation reads from accepted contracts rather than a discussion-only
proposal.

- Full test suite passes relative to the baseline recorded before the first

- Existing Step 08 standalone coordination behavior remains compatible.

Prefer additive changes in the existing ownership seams:

- `src/runner/definitions/` owns FlowDefinition schema/validation.

- General `addSessionEdge`.
- General peer mailbox or AgentMessage thread.

# Doer report — P02.2 (Phase 02 R5-R8: idempotency, context grant, bounds, driver authority)

Cell: P02.2 · Track: step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2 · Branch:
`step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2` (worked in place, nothing committed).

Proof Matrix and the mutation sweep, is in
`docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2/P02.2.md`;
this report covers what the cell brief asked for specifically — what was
built per requirement, how P02.1's exact bug class was avoided, the R8
interpretation, and what is genuinely left open.

## Files changed

Source (all under `src/runner/coordination/`):

- `store.mjs` (+139) — `authorizeOperation` gains three lock-held checks

  `assertWithinBindingInvocationCap`, called from `createSessionAssignment`'s

  grant-scope check in `authorizeDeclaredOperation`; the R6 gate (grant scope
  + context ceiling) inside `dispatchDeclaredOperation`'s driver-authorization
  block; `activation.maxInvocations` forwarded from both doors.
- `replay.mjs` (+15) — read-time duplicate-`invocationKey` parity.
- `schema.mjs` (8, doc comment only) — `validateAuthorizedBy`'s comment no
  longer says driver-authority is "a separate, later requirement"; it now
  points at where the check actually lives.

Tests:

- `test/runner/coordination-driver-authorization.test.mjs` (+463, 14 tests,
  20 → 34) — extended, not duplicated: reuses the existing
  `writeFixture`/`writeDefinition`/`fakeExecutor`/`setup`/`authorization`/
  `dispatch` scaffolding. `setup` gained an optional third `sessionOptions`
  argument; three small helpers added (`openSecondSession`, `dispatchProduce`,
  `rawAuthorize`).
- `test/runner/coordination-store.test.mjs` (+93, 2 tests, 38 → 40) — placed
  beside P02.1's own crash-state scaffolding, reusing its
  `writeUnregisteredClaim`/`authorizedProvenance`/`issueAuthorization`
  helpers. One fixture line changed (see R8 below).

Zero diff on every Do-Not-Touch path (`core/coordination-protocols/**`,
`src/runner/dispatch/**`, `cohort-planner.mjs`, `contracts/*.md`), and on
`current-cell.md` / `index.md` / P02.2.md's Review and Red-Team sections.
The whole diff is 816 insertions / 8 deletions, and all 8 deletions are
comment rewrites, one hoisted `readEvents` call, one widened test-helper
signature, and the one fixture id — no assertion weakened or removed.

## What was implemented, per requirement

### R5 — `invocationKey` consumed exactly once, session-scoped

Two enforcement points, both lock-held on a fresh from-disk read:

- **Issuance** (`authorizeOperation`): a second `operation-authorized` whose
  `invocationKey` already appears anywhere in this session's
  `events.jsonl` is refused. The scan is over the WHOLE session's
  authorizations, with no binding-triple filter — this is the contract's
  "checked against that session's own `events.jsonl`" read literally.
  Ordering matters and is deliberate: the pre-existing `authorizationId`
  idempotency early-return runs BEFORE the key check, so re-issuing an
  identical authorization is still a no-op rather than colliding with itself.
- **Consumption** (`assertAuthorizationSpendable`): an `assignment-created`
  carrying an `invocationKey` some OTHER Assignment already carries is
  refused, with the same `ownAssignmentId` exemption the sibling
  `authorizationId` check uses.

Plus read-time parity in `replay.mjs`, at exact structural parity with the
duplicate-`authorizationId` check three lines above it (`duplicate-ref`).

The crash/resume requirement is covered by the shape the contract actually
describes: the authorization lands, the process dies before any Assignment
exists, and on resume the driver's attempt to re-issue the same logical
invocation under a new `authorizationId` is refused as already issued — so
the resume spends the crashed attempt's own authorization and exactly one
Assignment materializes.

### R6 — context grant enforced at dispatch

`assertRefsOwnedBySession` is called in two places, and the second is the one
that makes this a gate rather than advice:

- In `authorizeDeclaredOperation`, so an out-of-session grant never reaches
  the log at all.
- In `dispatchDeclaredOperation`'s driver-authorization block, because the
  raw `store.authorizeOperation` door has no session-membership awareness and
  can put such a record on the log anyway. A test drives exactly that path.

The ceiling itself sits in that same block, between resolving the
authorization and `buildReadOnlyContract` — inside the ONLY producer of
`authorizationProvenance` in the codebase. Every resolved `contextRef` must
be in `grantedContextRefs`, with the single exception of the declared-edge
`fromAssignmentId`, which is structurally imposed by the topology and already
validated against the edge's declared `from` actor. There is no caller-facing
parameter that reaches the contract past this check.

### R7 — binding `maxInvocations`, counted fresh from disk

`activation.maxInvocations` is read only where the FlowDefinition is in hand
(`session-engine.mjs`) and enforced only where the lock is held
(`store.mjs`) — the same split the existing `maxAssignmentsForSession` /
`maxRoundsForSession` / `maxConcurrencyForSession` opts already use, extended
with the binding triple because a scalar cannot identify a binding.

Both layers count from the contract's named source — this session's on-disk
`operation-authorized` events for the exact `(nodeId, operationId,
targetActorId)` triple — inside the held `withEventsLock`. Issuance refuses
the (N+1)th authorization; dispatch refuses the (N+1)th materialization by
counting only authorizations already SPENT by an `assignment-created`,
excluding this call's own. The dispatch check is placed AFTER every
session-wide cap, so a stricter aggregate bound always refuses first — that
is what makes "binding caps narrow, never widen" true by placement rather
than by comment, and there is a test asserting the aggregate message fires
and the binding message provably does not.

### R8 — driver authority

`authorizedBy.id === manifest.provenanceRoot.writerId`, enforced lock-held in
`authorizeOperation`. See the interpretation section below.

## How P02.1's exact bug class was avoided

P02.1's HIGH-1 was: an invariant enforced in ONE of `createSessionAssignment`'s
two writing branches, so a crash into the self-heal shape reached around it.
The fix was a single shared helper, `assertAuthorizationSpendable`, called
from both branches inside the one `withEventsLock` critical section.

R5's dispatch-side check was therefore added **inside that same helper**, on
its existing single `readEvents`, carrying its existing `ownAssignmentId`
exemption — not as a parallel check somewhere else in the function. Concretely:

- There is still exactly one `assignment-created` append site
  (`completeAssignmentRegistration`), and still exactly two callers of it.
- Both callers still run `assertAuthorizationSpendable` first — the self-heal
  branch with `ownAssignmentId: claim.assignmentId`, the genuinely-new-taskKey
  branch with `undefined`.
- The new `invocationKey` check reads the same `events` array the
  `authorizationId` check does and applies the same exemption, so it cannot
  diverge from it and cannot be true on one branch and false on the other.
- The new R7 dispatch check deliberately runs only on the genuinely-new-taskKey
  path, alongside every other cap, so an idempotent resume is never counted as
  a fresh invocation — the same reasoning the existing caps document.

The regression test for this is driven on **both** writing paths explicitly
(`coordination-store.test.mjs`, "refuses provenance whose invocationKey
another Assignment already consumed, on BOTH writing paths"), built by
construction from P02.1's own crash-state helper rather than by concurrency,
exactly as P02.1's own regression tests were.

For R7, the analogous "second, differently-shaped check" trap would have been
a process-local counter. It is closed by test, not by claim: replacing the
disk count with a `Map` in the isolated copy left the in-process R7 test
PASSING and was caught by exactly one test — the cold-process one.

## R8 interpretation (the cell asked for this explicitly)

The accepted text gives two identities and no third: `authorizedBy` is
`{type: "driver", id: <driver-identity>}` where "the driver is not a

checked lock-held in `store.mjs`'s `authorizeOperation` — the single door
every authorization passes through, including the raw one, so there is no
lower-level door that skips it.

I did not treat the contract as insufficient (so this is not a BLOCKED

- This DOES close what P02.1 recorded. "Any caller able to reach
  `authorizeDeclaredOperation` can name an arbitrary driver id" is no longer

- This does NOT make the identity unforgeable. `writerId` is a self-declared

  opened the session can still present it. Making that impossible needs an
  authentication/attestation primitive that exists nowhere in this codebase,
  and adding one would be inventing contract semantics rather than
  implementing the accepted text — so I did not.

**Recommendation:** Review/Red-Team should rule explicitly on whether
pinning-without-attestation satisfies R8, or whether a follow-on phase owes a
real writer-identity primitive. The R8 text anticipates this question; I do
not think the Doer should answer it unilaterally.

Fixture consequence, which the cell predicted: `coordination-store.test.mjs`'s

`writer-1`. Changed to `writer-1` — one line plus a comment. That is exactly
the "existing test fixtures need updating to use a real, checkable driver
identity" case the Bug Taxonomy named as expected and fine.

# Doer report — P03.1 (Phase 03 R1-R4: artifact refs, recheck-as-new-Assignment, driver disposition, replay)

Cell: P03.1 · Track: step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2 · Branch:
`step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2` (worked in place, nothing committed).

All four requirements implemented with evidence. Full detail — Proof Matrix,
commands, mutation sweep, interpretations, gaps — is in
`docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2/P03.1.md`.
This report covers what the cell brief asks a Coordinator to read first: what
was built per requirement, the one decision that changed existing behavior
(and the two P02.2 tests it re-pointed), and what is left open.

## Files changed

Source (all under `src/runner/coordination/`):

- `schema.mjs` (+18/-5) — `driver-disposition-recorded` added to `EVENT_SPECS`
  with the contract's exact field table; `evidenceRefs` folded into the same
  array-shape branch `grantedContextRefs` already uses; `validateAuthorizedBy`
  reused verbatim (no second identity shape), its doc comment re-pointed at
  the now-shared store-side pin.
- `store.mjs` (+84/-16) — new `recordDriverDisposition` door, modeled on
  `authorizeOperation` line for line (validate shape → lock → manifest read →
  active check → driver-identity pin → idempotent append); new shared
  `assertDriverIdentity`, which is R8's `authorizedBy.id ===
  manifest.provenanceRoot.writerId` comparison EXTRACTED out of
  `authorizeOperation` so both doors run one check, not two copies.
- `session-engine.mjs` (+92/-7) — the R2 root-cause fix (below); one memoized
  `replaySession` per dispatch instead of up to two independent reads;
  `targetArtifactRef` scope-checked by the existing `assertRefsOwnedBySession`
  at both the authorize door and the dispatch gate.
- `replay.mjs` (+41) — `replaySession` additionally reconstructs `assignments`
  (dispatch provenance), `results` (result links, in order), and
  `dispositions`.

Tests:

- `test/runner/coordination-recheck-disposition.test.mjs` (new, 14 tests) —
  R1-R4, positive and negative, against a project-tier fixture and a real
  subprocess executor (same harness discipline as the sibling files).
- `test/runner/coordination-driver-authorization.test.mjs` (41 → 42 tests) —
  two silent-discard guard tests re-pointed (below) plus one new companion
  test.

Do-Not-Touch surfaces (`core/coordination-protocols/`, `src/runner/dispatch/`,
`src/verbs/coordination/`, the accepted contracts, `cohort-planner.mjs`):
`git diff --stat` empty. `src/verbs/coordination/{run,show}.mjs` were read
only, as the brief's May Inspect allows.

## What was built, per requirement

**R1 — artifact refs.** No new artifact mechanism, deliberately: artifact refs
already exist end to end as `runResult.evidence.artifacts` (produced by
`dispatch/assignment-runner.mjs`, returned to every caller by
`dispatchDeclaredOperation`), rooted under the producing Assignment's own run
directory. The session's job is to LINK them, which
`operation-authorized.targetArtifactRef` and `contextGrant.refs` already do.
The only code R1 needed was making `targetArtifactRef` obey the same
same-session rule the grant does, at both doors — which also closes P02.2's
Red-Team LOW-1 at exactly the moment it said to ("Phase 03's recheck semantics
are what will start reading it"). The test asserts the session directory is
still exactly `{events.jsonl, session.json, tasks}` before AND after a full
grant-plus-recheck cycle, so "not a second artifact authority" is proven, not
asserted.

**R2 — recheck is a new Assignment.** This is the real fix for the
taskKey-derivation gap P02.2 recorded. A driver-authorized invocation's
DEFAULT claim key now carries the id of the authorization it spends:
`declared:<operationId>[:round-N]:auth:<authorizationId>`. Because
`authorizeOperation` already refuses to issue two authorizations under one id
(and one `invocationKey`), two invocations at one binding structurally cannot
be claim-equal — and neither can ever equal a key derived from
`nodeId`+`operationId`+`actorId` alone, which is the shape the contract's
"Recheck Is Not Retry" clause names as forbidden. That forbidden shape is
tested literally: a recheck dispatched with the ORIGINAL review binding's own
default key is REFUSED (by P02.2's silent-discard guard, unchanged), the
original Assignment untouched, the authorization left unconsumed.

The ordering problem this had to solve: the taskKey is what a claim record is
looked up BY, so the authorization cannot be resolved the usual way (which
needs the resumed Assignment id) before the key exists. Resolved with a
separate, small selector (`resolveTaskKeyAuthorization`): prefer an unconsumed
authorization (the invocation being spent), else the most recent consumed one
(a repeat/crash resume, which must land on the key its own invocation first
claimed). The dispatch gate below is untouched and re-resolves exactly as
before. Both resume shapes are covered by test — an idempotent repeat and the
crash-recovery self-heal Red-Team built for P02.2 — and both still pass.

Recheck never supersedes: the original's `result.json` is compared
byte-for-byte before and after, `run-retried` count is asserted 0 (so
`linkResult`'s `allowSupersede` path is provably never entered), and each
Assignment has exactly one `result-linked`.

**R3 — disposition.** A new store door, not a RunResult field and not a worker
Assignment. It mirrors `authorizeOperation` structurally, and its identity
check is literally the same function as R8's — extracted and shared rather
than copied, which is what the Bug Taxonomy asked for. The "never a worker
result" property is shown two ways: the worker's own `result.json` is asserted
not to contain the string at all, and `validateEventPayload('result-linked',
{..., disposition})` is asserted to REJECT the field, so there is no
result-shaped event a worker could smuggle one through.

**R4 — replay.** `replaySession` now also returns `assignments`, `results`,
and `dispositions`. Recheck lineage is the join
`assignments[].authorizationId → authorizations[].targetArtifactRef` (which
artifact revision each Assignment ran against; the original first-pass review
carries no `authorizationId` at all). "From `events.jsonl`/`session.json`
alone" is asserted literally: every answer is re-derived a second time
straight from `readSessionEvents` + `readManifest` and asserted equal.

## The one behavior change, and the two tests it re-pointed

Making the default taskKey carry the authorization id means the two collision
shapes P02.2's silent-discard guard was built for are no longer reachable by
OMITTING a taskKey — which is the root-cause fix P02.2 explicitly deferred to
this phase. Two of its tests drove the collision that way and would otherwise
have failed for the right reason.

Both were re-pointed to a caller-supplied shared `taskKey`, the one way the
collision is still reachable, so the guard keeps exactly the coverage the
Reviewer and Red-Team mutation-verified (mutation-checked again here: both
still fail if the guard is disabled). Nothing was weakened — a NEW test proves
the default path now SUCCEEDS where it used to be refused: a fan-out with no
explicit taskKey materializes two Assignments, one per authorization, each
carrying its own `authorizationId`.

## Verification

- Focused glob `flow-definition*` + `coordination*`: **365/365** (was 350).
- Full suite, clean run: **5131 tests, 5119 pass, 7 fail** — exactly baseline
  #1-#7 by name, zero coordination/definitions failures. Count 5116 → 5131 is
  precisely this cell's 15 new tests. The other full run of this cell also
  carried three live/cross-process timing failures (gateway lock, herdr-spawn
  idle, lock-wait), each re-run in isolation and passing, none importing from
  `src/runner/coordination/**` — the load-induced-flake pattern this track has
  now recorded four times.
- Mutation sweep, isolated copy, 9 mutations: every one caught, each by the
  dedicated test meant to catch it (table in `P03.1.md`). Copy deleted; the
  real tree re-verified green after.
- Impact-analysis gate: `fgos tool query --capability impact-analysis --status
  present` returns `providers: []` → **Inactive** posture, no evidence owed.
  Blast radius cross-checked by grep instead: `replaySession` has no consumer
  outside `src/runner/coordination/**`; `dispatchDeclaredOperation`'s
  signature is unchanged and its one external caller forwards an OPTIONAL
  taskKey; no shipped fixture declares `activation`, so every change here
  stays structurally unreachable for shipped configs.

## Open / for the Coordinator to rule on

Everything below is recorded in full in `P03.1.md`'s Gaps section; these are
the ones worth a decision rather than a read.

1. **`disposition` is validated as a non-empty string, not a closed enum.**
   The contract says "e.g. `accepted | rejected`" and also describes "closing
   a round," so shape-only is the literal read. One line to close if Review
   wants a fixed vocabulary. Note this is a DIFFERENT mechanism from
   `session-engine.mjs`'s pre-existing `DISPOSITION_VALUES`, which governs the
   Phase 04 consult-disposition Assignment, not this event.
2. **No session-scope check on a disposition's `targetRef`/`evidenceRefs`.**
   Inert today — nothing reads them into a contract, prompt, or gate — so this
   follows the same "close it when it is read" posture that
   `targetArtifactRef` was held to (and which this cell now discharges for
   that field). If any future surface renders dispositions into worker-visible
   context, the check belongs there first.
3. **Post-terminal dispositions are refused at write time but not neutralized
   at read time**, unlike `operation-authorized`. Deliberate: Recovery Rule
   point 5's neutralization exists so a post-terminal authorization can never
   satisfy the dispatch gate, and a disposition has no gate and materializes
   nothing — discarding a durable driver decision found on the log would lose
   information for no safety gain.
4. **Concurrency is argued from construction plus deterministic tests, not a
   real multi-process reproduction** — the class this track's history says
   sequential tests miss. The specific race worth attacking: two concurrent
   dispatchers with ONE unconsumed authorization now derive the SAME taskKey
   (they must — that is the resume property), so they collide on one claim
   exactly as two same-taskKey callers always have; expected outcome is one
   Assignment plus one refusal/resume, never two.
5. **The shipped-fixture fan-out HIGH is NOT covered by this fix.** The
   authorization-derived suffix applies only to `driver-authorized` bindings;
   a `required` topology-edge dispatch has no authorization to key on, so
   `independent-research-fan-out-fan-in.yaml`'s collision still needs
   `targetActorId` threaded into the topology-edge derivation, exactly as
   `index.md` records. Said explicitly here so nobody reads this cell as
   having closed it.
6. **R5-R7 remain P03.2's**, by this cell's own Non-Goals: no live CLI/no-Work
   run, no consolidated negative-proof battery, no surface-readiness doc.
   `replaySession`'s new return shape is what `show.mjs` will read.

# Doer report — P03.2 (Phase 03 R5-R7: live CLI no-Work proof, negative-proof battery, surface readiness)

Cell: P03.2 · Track: step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2 · Branch:
`step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2` (worked in place, nothing committed).

All three requirements implemented with evidence. Full detail — Proof
Matrix, the 17-row contract-bullet cross-reference, the verbatim live run,
mutation sweep, interpretations, gaps — is in
`docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2/P03.2.md`.
This report covers what a Coordinator should read first: **one decision
that needs your ruling**, what was built, and what is left open.

## READ FIRST — the one shared-fixture change (escalated, RULED, closed)

`core/coordination-protocols/standalone-master-coordination-loop.yaml` was
changed by this cell. Reviewer and Red-Team will look here first, so:

**Why it was mandatory, not a preference.**
`session-engine.mjs:1074-1080` refuses to authorize any binding whose
activation mode is not `driver-authorized`. The fixture declared no
`activation` at all, so no `operation-authorized` event could ever be
written for it — making R5's "authorized revision, authorized recheck" and
R6's "unauthorized optional operation refused through the CLI door" both
**structurally unreachable** against the file R5's acceptance names.

**Before → after:** all six bindings were implicitly `required`. Three now
declare `activation: {mode: driver-authorized}` — `revise-candidate`
(`phase-revision`), `reviewer-recheck` and `red-team-recheck`
(`phase-recheck`). The first pass (`produce-candidate`,
`review-candidate`, `red-team-candidate`) is **unchanged at `required`**.
The header paragraph explaining "there is no `activation` field yet" was
replaced, since Phase 02 shipped that field and the statement was false.
Nothing else changed: same operations, actors, nodes, transitions;
`metadata.version` left at `1.0.0` (reasoning flagged in `P03.2.md`'s
Gaps).

**Blast radius, measured:** `git grep` finds exactly two non-doc consumers
(`flow-definition-standalone-master-coordination-loop.test.mjs`,
`flow-definition-protocol-loader.test.mjs`); neither asserts on
`activation`; both pass unchanged (58/58). No source module references the
fixture by id. Mutation M6 proves the change is load-bearing: removing
`activation` from just the `reviewer-recheck` binding fails the
fixture-shape test and both full live-proof runs.

**Authority — settled.** The cell brief's Do Not Touch list names only the
other three yaml fixtures and deliberately omits this one; its Must Read
told the Doer to check this exact field and treat its absence as this
cell's own concern. The dispatching Agent prompt carried a broader
blanket line that contradicted this. Reported to the Coordinator with
evidence and three options before the edit; **Coordinator ruled Option A**
— make the change, keep the first pass at `required`, and confirmed the
dispatch-prompt line was overly-broad shorthand with `current-cell.md`
authoritative. Full record in `P03.2.md`'s "Deliberate shipped-fixture
change" section and its Gaps.

## The second gap the cell had to close (the one the brief named)

`run.mjs` had no way to call `authorizeDeclaredOperation` or
`recordDriverDisposition`. Closed by two new `steps[]` types on the
existing request shape — no new CLI subcommand, no new verb:

| `type` | Reaches | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `authorize` | `authorizeDeclaredOperation` (session-engine) | `operationId`, `targetActorId?`, `nodeId?`, `authorizationId`, `invocationKey`, `reason`, `grantedContextRefs?`, `targetArtifactRef?` |
| `disposition` | `recordDriverDisposition` (store) | `targetRef`, `disposition`, `rationale`, `evidenceRefs?` |

Two design points worth your attention:

- **`authorizedBy` is refused, not accepted.** The engine pins both events
  to `manifest.provenanceRoot.writerId`, which is the request's own
  top-level `writerId`, so a request-file `authorizedBy` could only ever
  agree or be refused deeper down — a field with no independent effect,
  exactly what `run.mjs`'s existing fan-out-policy refusal pattern
  forbids. It is refused at the schema boundary with a message naming the
  single real channel. Every other field I accept provably reaches an
  engine call (mutation-proven).
- **`run.mjs` now imports `store.mjs` directly**, for
  `recordDriverDisposition` only — its header comment previously said it
  never does. There is no definition-aware disposition door in
  `session-engine.mjs` to delegate to, and `session-engine.mjs` is Do Not
  Touch for this cell. `store.mjs`'s door is complete on its own (shape
  validation, active-session check, driver-identity pin, lock-held
  idempotent append). I updated the header comment to name the exception
  honestly rather than route around it. If you want the rule back
  literally, it is a one-line re-export from `session-engine.mjs`.

## Files changed

Source:

- `src/verbs/coordination/schema.mjs` (+91/-1) — `validateAuthorizeStep`,
  `validateDispositionStep`, `assertNoAuthorizedBy`, and the `type`
  dispatch in `validateSteps` (now four types, message updated).
- `src/verbs/coordination/run.mjs` (+72) — two new branches in the
  declared-protocol step loop; `driverIdentity` derived from
  `request.writerId`; `$ref:` resolution extended to
  `grantedContextRefs`/`targetArtifactRef`/`targetRef`/`evidenceRefs`
  through the SAME `resolveRef`/`resolveRefArray` the existing steps use;
  header comment updated for the `store.mjs` exception.
- `core/coordination-protocols/standalone-master-coordination-loop.yaml`
  (+14/-13) — the activation change above (see READ FIRST), Coordinator-ruled.

  Gaps in `P03.2.md`).

Tests (both new, 23 tests):

- `test/verbs/coordination-run-driver-steps.test.mjs` (19) — 9 request-
  boundary reject/normalize cases, then 10 real end-to-end runs through
  `runCoordinationUseCase` against a project-tier fixture and a real
  Node-subprocess executor.
- `test/verbs/coordination-run-live-proof.test.mjs` (4) — the R5 live
  proof: a genuinely spawned `fgos coordination run` subprocess against
  the SHIPPED core-tier fixture, plus the fixture-shape assertion and two
  live negatives.

Docs:

- `docs/architect/.../step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2/P03.2.md` (new).
- `docs/architect/.../step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2/thin-launcher-surface-readiness.md`
  (new) — R7. No skill file, slash command, or CLI subcommand created.
- One link line each added to
  `docs/architect/agent-coordination/architecture/coordination-foundation-baseline.md`
  and `docs/architect/proposals/step-09-group-thinking-substrate.md`
  (R5's "final docs point to the verification index" acceptance item —
  neither linked it before; both are outside the file list you gave me,
  flagged here for that reason).

Do-Not-Touch surfaces confirmed at **zero diff** by
`git diff --stat`: `src/runner/**`, all contract files, the three other
`core/coordination-protocols/*.yaml` fixtures, and `show.mjs`.

Note, not mine: `docs/architect/agent-coordination/playbooks/{coordination-operating-harness.md,prompts/master-coordinator.md}`
show as modified in the working tree. I never opened them.

## R5 — the live proof, in one line each

One real `fgos coordination run --file master-loop.json` subprocess, exit
0, session `coord_master_loop_live`, protocol
`core.coordination-protocol.standalone-master-coordination-loop@1.0.0`,
final `status: "completed"` / `closed: true` / `quorum.missing: []`.

Eleven steps in one request file: produce → review + red-team (required)
→ **authorize** revision → revise → **rejecting** disposition →
**authorize** reviewer recheck → reviewer recheck → **authorize**
red-team recheck → red-team recheck → **accepting** disposition → close.
Six Assignments, six `result-linked`, three `operation-authorized`, two
`driver-disposition-recorded`, **zero `run-retried`** (so the original
review's RunResult is provably never superseded by its recheck). Every
cross-step ref is a `$ref:<label>` placeholder resolved at dispatch time —
no Assignment id is knowable when the request file is written, which is
the whole reason a static request can express this loop.

**No Work, no git, no repo mutation**, measured three ways in the test and

and after, `stateView` deep-equal (`{"work":{},"decisions":[]}`), no

`coordinationId` on the Assignments).

## R6 — cross-reference, not a rewrite

All 17 bullets of `coordination-session.md`'s "Required Negative Tests"
are tabulated in `P03.2.md`, each with its covering test named. **Four
were genuine gaps and got new tests** (bullets 1, 13, 14, 16 — two
concurrent sessions under one writer; unauthorized optional operation at
the CLI door; `invocationKey` reuse at the CLI door; hidden context at the
CLI door). Bullets 13/14/16 were already proven at the ENGINE door by
P00-P03.1; what was missing was the door this cell opens. Three more
(4, 7, 17) are additionally re-asserted inside the live proof and are
explicitly **not** claimed as new coverage. The remaining ten were read
and confirmed already covered — no test was written that duplicates them.

## Verification

- Focused: `'test/runner/flow-definition*' 'test/runner/coordination*'
  'test/verbs/coordination*' 'test/cli/coordination*'` → **423/423 pass**
  (400 → 423, exactly the 23 new tests).
- Full suite: **5157 tests, 5144 pass, 8 fail, 5 skipped** (5134 → 5157,
  exactly +23). Seven failures are baseline #1-#7 by name; baseline #8
  (`herdr-spawn LIVE`) passed. The eighth is `glm-cli executor (LIVE)` —

# Reviewer Report — Cell P00.1 (Contract Promotion)

Track: step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2
Cell: P00.1
Reviewer: independent (no access to Doer's own reasoning; diff/contracts/proposal read directly)

## Verdict

1 MEDIUM, 2 LOW findings. No HIGH findings.

Full findings recorded in
`docs/architect/agent-coordination/verification/step-09-group-thinking-mvp1-mvp2/P00.1.md`
under `## Review`.

## Summary

- Independently reconfirmed (not trusting the Doer's Commands section):
  `git diff --check` clean on all 4 named files; zero diff on
  `group-cognition-framework.yaml` and `assignment-run-runresult.md`; zero
  diff on `step-09-group-thinking-substrate.md`, `architecture-intent.md`,
  and `component-authority-boundary-map.md`; `git status --porcelain` shows
  only the 3 intended doc files modified, no `src/`/`test/`/`core/` touched.
- Content faithfulness against substrate §6-9: `operation-authorized`,
  `driver-disposition-recorded`, `invocationKey` idempotency, context-grant
  enforcement, and recheck-vs-retry semantics all match the substrate's
  concrete shapes (JSON examples in §7, Bounds rule, gap table in §9). No
  MVP6-9 concepts (deliberation memory, visibility windows, richer
  aggregation, `addSessionEdge`) leaked into accepted text — confirmed
  absent from the diff.
- Component authority claim (R3, "no edit needed") independently
  re-verified against `component-authority-boundary-map.md` §6 lines
  171-184 directly, not just the Doer's cited line numbers — confirmed
  correct as-is.
- All 7 required negative-test scenarios present in both contracts'
  Required Negative Tests sections.
- Anchors: hand-computed the GitHub slug for the new
  `## Driver-Authorized Optional Operations And Recheck (MVP1/MVP2, Step 09)`
  heading and confirmed `flow-definition.md`'s cross-reference to it
  resolves exactly; all other new/changed relative links resolve to real
  files.

## Findings

1. **MEDIUM** — The scope disclaimer repeated in both contracts ("This
   section does NOT accept ... (Step 09 MVP3+/MVP6-9) — those stay
   deferred/discussion") literally excludes "MVP3+", but the substrate's
   own MVP Plan table (§8) labels "Recheck and disposition" as MVP3 — and
   that is exactly the content the same section promotes as accepted. The
   ambiguity traces back to the cell brief's own bundling of recheck/
   disposition under "MVP1/MVP2," so it's not a Doer invention, but the
   promoted text had the opportunity to resolve the resulting
   contradiction and didn't. Smallest fix: narrow the parenthetical to
   `(Step 09 MVP6-9)` or add one disambiguating clause, in both files.

2. **LOW** — `targetArtifactRef` (used in the promoted contract) vs.
   `artifactRevision` (used in substrate §8/§9's gap-table prose) is an
   inconsistency in the source material itself; the Doer picked the name
   matching substrate §7's concrete JSON example, which is a reasonable
   call, but did so silently with no cross-reference note.

3. **LOW** — The added cross-reference sentence in
   `coordination-foundation-baseline.md` paraphrases the substance of
   `master-coordinator.md`'s Runtime Boundary section ("manual-only,"
   "never loaded as runtime authority") rather than being a bare pointer,
   which is accurate today but has no sync mechanism if the source wording
   changes later.

Two claims were checked and explicitly rejected as non-issues (see the
"Verified and rejected as non-issues" subsection in `P00.1.md`'s Review):
the `authorizedBy` field added to `driver-disposition-recorded` (justified
by substrate §9's Driver authority row), and the three-aggregate-bound
phrasing of the binding-cap-never-widens rule (justified by substrate §7's
full Bounds rule paragraph, not just its summary sentence).

Status: DONE
Summary: Reviewed cell P00.1's contract promotion diff independently against the substrate proposal, component-authority map, and protected-file zero-diff requirements; found 1 MEDIUM (self-contradictory MVP3+ scope disclaimer vs. substrate's own MVP numbering for the promoted recheck/disposition content) and 2 LOW (silent field-naming divergence; cross-reference sentence paraphrases rather than purely points) findings, no HIGH findings, and no invariant/scope-leakage/protected-file violations.
Concerns/Blockers: None blocking — all findings are documentation-clarity issues, not content or invariant defects.
